newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South Africa's rand and bond markets gave the thumbs up to Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's maiden budget on Wednesday as both ended sharply firmer.
At 1400 GMT, the rand was quoted at 4.4170/4200 against the dollar from 4.4300/4330 overnight, while the key R150 was pegged at 14.74 percent from 14.795 percent on Tuesday.
While traders and analysts hailed the overall budget as positive, they cited Manuel's announcement on the further relaxation of exchange controls as the main reason for the market exuberance.
"I think the move to allow residents to hold foreign currency accounts is very positive. Broadening the asset swap mechanism is also very positive," Mathison and Hollidge economist Henry Flint said.
The rand reacted almost immediately to the news, firming to 4.4160 bid within 20 minutes of the announcement.
But importers looking to cover tempered the market's initial enthusiasm and promptly hauled the currency back to the 4.43 level 10 minutes later.
"I think a few guys saw it moving back to levels they saw on Tuesday and decided to start buying (dollars)," a trader said.
That was followed by more dollars sales which helped the currency to its closing level.
Dealers said the rand was likely to score more gains on Thursday.

"Overall I think (the budget) is positive and I would think we could test the lower levels tomorrow," one trader said. "The market seems to be long and offshore seems to want to sell dollars," she said, adding that a 4.40 to 4.45 range was expected on Thursday.
The rand's strength against the dollar helped it to its strongest level against sterling since September 25, as it moved to just above the 7.0 level from 7.1279/1371 overnight.
Against the mark it was last quoted at 0.3862/3866 from 0.3848/3852 previously.
Traders on the bond market were equally bullish about the budget, although profit-taking shortly after Manuel's budget presentation began tempered the market's initial enthusiasm.

Dealers said the market's initial rally, which pushed the R150 to 14.755 percent within 20 minutes of the start of Manuel's speech, stemmed from short-covering by players who had gone into the budget short.
"Everyone was expecting a positive budget so they started going short before it and then covered their positions afterwards," a bond trader said.
Another trader pointed to the fact that government's funding plans were in line with expectations as one of the major factors which fuelled already bullish sentiment.
Profit-taking set in at around the 14.76 level, pulling rates back up to the 14.84 percent level before buyers returned.
Eric Wood, chief bond trader at Investec Merchant Bank, said the market also retraced amid some disappointement that there had been no change to pension fund taxation.
"We were expecting a change in the tax on income to a tax on total assets, which would shift the current preference towards investment in equities," Wood said.
Overall, however, Wood felt the budget was positive.
Dealers said bonds looked set to make further gains on Thursday in the wake of what most traders described as a very positive budget.
On the money market, three-month deposit were steady at between 16.50 and 16.55 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate held its recent 16.10 to 15.90 percent range.
The Reserve Bank indicated the money market shortage slightly easier at 11.147 billion rand on Tuesday from 11.171 billion rand on Monday.
The Bond Exchange said foreigners were net buyers of a hefty 525.13 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Tuesday after buying 68.21 million rand's worth on Monday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 6.4 billion rand on Tuesday from 4.86 billion rand.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
